C-SYSTEM-UPDATE-COMPATIBILITY-20260907.Summary: Implement a separately trusted, crash-safe core and engine update lane with authenticated immutable artifacts, compatibility negotiation, independently bootable fallback, optional-feature quarantine, and preserved user data.
C-SYSTEM-UPDATE-COMPATIBILITY-20260907.Problem: Feature activation and core or engine replacement have different trust, distribution, boot, and rollback risks. Combining them makes the first programmable-feature proof depend on release infrastructure while leaving privileged updater authority insufficiently isolated.

Goals.Goal: Give one verified system updater principal exclusive authority to stage core and engine candidates without making it callable or configurable by ordinary features.
Authenticate update metadata and artifacts, validate platform and compatibility, and stage an independently bootable fallback before selection.
Negotiate feature ABI, capability contract, state schema, native IPC, engine profile, and rollback compatibility independently.
Disable or quarantine incompatible optional features while preserving their immutable packages and installation-owned data.
Project update identity, phase, compatibility, failure, and recovery actions through protected host-owned UI state.
Recover deterministically from crash or power loss at every durable update transition.

Constraints.Constraint: SPEC APPROVAL DOES NOT APPROVE A PLAN OR IMPLEMENTATION.
C-PLATFORM-DURABLE-PACKAGE-ACTIVATION-20260906, C-FEATURE-TRANSACTIONAL-ACTIVATION-SLICE-20260906, and C-PLATFORM-NETWORK-EGRESS-CONFINEMENT-20260907 must be applied before this change is planned.
Ordinary features cannot invoke, reconfigure, impersonate, supply trust roots to, or draw consent UI for the updater.
Updater traffic uses a dedicated egress authority and cannot reuse ordinary feature, model-provider, integration, or browser-navigation grants.
No update is selected without authenticated metadata, artifact digest, correct platform, compatibility decision, and an independently bootable fallback.
An old engine cannot automatically open a profile after an irreversible schema migration; rollback compatibility is explicit and fail closed.
Protected updater and recovery state cannot depend on optional feature code or feature-owned storage.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Public release publishing or organization-wide release operations.
Hot-swapping engines inside a live browsing session.
Automatic downgrade across incompatible persistent schemas.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A distinct trusted updater principal is the only authority permitted to stage core or engine candidates and is unreachable through ordinary feature capability invocation.

Tests reject unauthenticated metadata, digest mismatch, wrong platform, downgrade attack, incompatible feature ABI, incompatible native IPC, rollback-incompatible state, and missing fallback before switch.
Failpoints and fresh-process restart at every durable transition recover to exactly one bootable current candidate or the independently verified fallback.
An engine profile change disables or quarantines only incompatible optional features while preserving their packages and installation-owned data.
Mandatory browsing, stop, update, quarantine, and recovery composition boots without executing optional user code after a bad candidate.
Updater egress, metadata verification, artifact staging, selection, boot health, promotion, and rollback have separate recorded outcomes and no blind retry after an uncertain external effect.
Operational telemetry records release and artifact identifiers, phase, compatibility outcome, timing, and failure class without credentials, page content, profile data, or raw user payloads.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh artifact-tamper, compatibility, kill-and-restart, bad-engine, optional-feature-quarantine, fallback-boot, and real updater-egress evidence proves that system update is isolated from ordinary feature authority and cannot strand the product without a trusted boot path.

Assumptions.Assumption: The feature package catalog supplies reusable immutable artifact and compatibility primitives without granting its activation authority to the updater.
The first update lane can use a bounded release trust model before public transparency and key-rotation policy are designed.
